Carmen Delgado’s recent work on AWS cost optimization for NebulaTech’s core platform stands out. She identified a 25% overprovisioning leak in their EC2 clusters and rearchitected the infrastructure using Terraform, reducing monthly spend by $120K while improving deployment consistency. Her Ansible playbooks streamlined multi-environment syncs, cutting manual errors by 40% during a critical scaling event.  

Carmen joined NebulaTech as a Linux admin but quickly transitioned into platform engineering, mastering CI/CD pipelines and Kubernetes orchestration. She built a unified deployment framework that integrated Docker and Prometheus, enabling automated scaling during their first major product launch. Her ability to balance operational reliability with rapid innovation made her a key driver of their cloud migration.  

When NebulaTech faced a surge in traffic during a security audit, Carmen spearheaded a chaos engineering exercise. She simulated AWS region outages and API throttling, exposing bottlenecks in their monitoring stack. Her fixes—refining alert thresholds and adding redundant Kubernetes nodes—boosted system resilience without compromising SLA compliance.  

Beyond technical contributions, Carmen mentors junior engineers in Terraform and cloud cost modeling. She’s also bridged gaps between dev and ops teams by standardizing infrastructure-as-code practices. Her calm under pressure and knack for turning ambiguity into actionable insights make her a dependable collaborator.  

Carmen’s technical depth, problem-solving agility, and leadership in cross-functional teams align closely with the values of a high-performing platform engineer. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss her potential further.
